title: Tailwind v4 CLI auto-scans the whole project for candidate classes by default
cause: Without an explicit source configuration, @import "tailwindcss" makes the CLI heuristically scan every file in the project (respecting .gitignore) for strings that look like Tailwind classes and compiles CSS for them - including string literals inside Python test files/docstrings, not just template/JS files.
fix: Use @import "tailwindcss" source(none); plus an explicit @source pointing only at the intended content file(s). Verified: a security-test string "bg-[url(evil)]" in a pytest file got compiled into the output before source(none) was added; confirmed absent after.

title: Debian bookworm's apt nodejs package is too old for Tailwind v4
cause: apt-cache policy nodejs on the ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim image resolves to 18.20.4, but Tailwind v4 (@tailwindcss/cli) requires Node 20+.
fix: Install Node 20 from NodeSource in the Docker builder stage (curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - && apt-get install -y nodejs) instead of apt's default nodejs package. The base image also lacks curl/ca-certificates/gnupg - install those first.

title: Tailwind v4's default color palette renders as oklch(), not rgb()
cause: Tailwind v4 switched its default color palette to the OKLCH color space. getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor for a class like bg-blue-500 returns "oklch(0.623 0.214 259.815)", not an rgb(...) string.
fix: When asserting on computed colors in browser tests (Playwright etc.) against Tailwind v4 output, expect oklch(...) strings, not rgb(...). Verified via a real Playwright run against a live editor page.

title: tests/test_ai_transform.py's happy-path test hits the real configured AI_PROVIDER, not a fake
cause: test_valid_request_returns_operations doesn't mock EditorAIService.stream_generate_operations, so it goes through to whatever AI_PROVIDER is set in .env (e.g. opencode_zen, a real live model) - the model occasionally proposes something the server-side validator rejects (invalid_operations), which is expected AI-output variance, not a code bug. This makes the test flaky in any environment where .env configures a real provider.
fix: Don't treat this test's occasional failure as a regression signal without first checking the actual rejection reason (views.py's invalid_operations log now includes it, see the wizard_service.py precedent for that pattern). To make this test deterministic, mock the provider like every other test in the file already does.

title: Django collectstatic/WhiteNoise post-processing fails on build-source CSS files inside STATICFILES_DIRS
error_message: whitenoise.storage.MissingFileError: The file 'editor/tailwindcss' could not be found
cause: CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage post-processes every collected CSS file looking for relative url()/@import references to rewrite. A Tailwind build-source file (tailwind-input.css, containing @import "tailwindcss") sitting inside STATICFILES_DIRS gets treated as a real static asset and fails post-processing since "tailwindcss" isn't a real relative file.
fix: Exclude build-source files from collectstatic with --ignore=<filename> (e.g. --ignore=tailwind-input.css --ignore=.tailwind-safelist.txt) - they're compiled into a real output file (tailwind.css) that IS meant to be collected normally.

title: DRF BooleanField treats an absent key as False for multipart/form data, not the model default
cause: DRF's BooleanField has HTML-checkbox-convention handling: for multipart/form-encoded requests, an absent boolean field is coerced to False (mimicking an unchecked HTML checkbox) instead of being omitted from validated_data (which is what happens for a plain JSON request, letting the model's own default apply). A product-creation form that uploads a file (forcing multipart) silently created every product as is_active=False even though the model default is True and the field was never touched.
fix: Declare the field explicitly with an explicit default on the serializer (e.g. is_active = serializers.BooleanField(required=False, default=True)) instead of relying on ModelSerializer's auto-generated field + the model's own default=True. Only bites when the request uses multipart/form-data (e.g. because of an accompanying file upload) - a pure JSON POST to the same endpoint does not trigger it, which is why it's easy to miss in JSON-only tests.

title: Stripe webhook signature verification works fully offline, no network needed
cause: stripe.Webhook.construct_event(payload, sig_header, webhook_secret) performs a local HMAC computation against the raw payload and webhook_secret - it never calls the Stripe API. This means signature-rejection behavior can be unit-tested directly (a bogus sig_header against any secret_key raises stripe.error.SignatureVerificationError) without any real API key, test-mode or otherwise.
fix: Test the invalid-signature rejection path directly against StripePaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event with a fake secret_key/sig_header - no need to skip this test or gate it behind real Stripe credentials.

title: Tailwind max-w-* has a named container-width scale separate from the numeric spacing scale
error_message: AI produced invalid operations for user 40: disallowed Tailwind class: max-w-4xl
cause: apps/ai_assistant/tailwind_classes.py's UTILITY_FAMILIES only mapped max-w to SIZING_SCALE (the numeric px/rem-based scale shared with w/h/min-w/etc), but Tailwind's max-w-* utility also has its own named scale (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl..7xl, full, min, max, fit, prose, none) used for page/content containers. max-w-4xl is one of the most common Tailwind classes for a page wrapper and was rejected outright, surfacing as a confusing AI 'invalid changes' error unrelated to what the user actually asked for.
fix: Added MAX_WIDTH_NAMED_SCALE and set UTILITY_FAMILIES["max-w"] = SIZING_SCALE | MAX_WIDTH_NAMED_SCALE. Deliberately left w/min-w/h/min-h/max-h on the numeric scale only, since the named scale is a max-w-specific Tailwind convention (w-4xl is not a real Tailwind class).

title: A user-reported AI rejection screenshot can have a misleading apparent cause - always check the server log for the real error string
cause: A screenshot showing 'La IA propuso cambios no válidos' for a YouTube-embed instruction looked like an iframe-rejection bug at a glance, but the actual server log (apps/ai_assistant/views.py's logger.warning) showed the real cause was 'disallowed Tailwind class: max-w-4xl' - a completely unrelated Tailwind allowlist gap the model happened to hit in the same generation attempt. Only after fixing that and re-running the exact original instruction did the real second cause (iframe fully forbidden) surface.
fix: Never fix the surface-level guess from a screenshot alone. Reproduce the exact instruction against a real server and read the structured log line the view already emits (user id + exact rejection reason) before writing any fix.

title: iframe embeds enabled for YouTube/Vimeo only, restricted by src prefix allowlist
cause: iframe was in sanitize.py's FORBIDDEN_TAGS entirely (security: arbitrary iframe src on a now-publicly-published page is a clickjacking/phishing vector), which silently blocked the common, legitimate request to embed a YouTube video with no clear error message to the end user.
fix: Removed iframe from FORBIDDEN_TAGS but added a tag-specific check in sanitize_node: iframe's src attribute must start with one of IFRAME_SRC_ALLOWED_PREFIXES (youtube.com/embed/, youtube-nocookie.com/embed/, player.vimeo.com/video/). Also updated the AI system prompt (prompts.py) to convert youtube watch URLs to embed URLs and to use aspect-video + absolute inset-0 w-full h-full instead of an arbitrary pb-[56.25%] padding-hack, which the model tried first and which the Tailwind allowlist correctly rejects (no arbitrary values supported).

title: Server-side iframe allowlist fix alone doesn't make embeds visible - CSP and client-side renderer have their own separate copies
cause: After fixing apps/ai_assistant/sanitize.py to allow YouTube/Vimeo iframe src, the user still couldn't see the embedded video in the editor preview. Two more, independent blockers existed: (1) the CSP header (frame-src 'self' in both config/settings/development.py and production.py) silently blocked the nested cross-origin frame in the browser with no visible error unless checking console/network; (2) static/editor/editor-core.js's own client-side renderNode() has a SEPARATE, hand-maintained forbiddenTags set (historically kept in sync manually with sanitize.py, per CLAUDE.md's note not to refactor this file) that dropped <iframe> unconditionally regardless of src.
fix: Any tag/attribute allowlist change touching client-visible rendering must be checked in THREE places for this project: apps/ai_assistant/sanitize.py (server validation), static/editor/editor-core.js's renderNode (client preview), and the CSP frame-src/img-src/etc directives (config/settings/development.py + production.py) - a fix in only one silently fails downstream with no clear error.
